nodes.title: Master
nodes.description: Master seed. Any text or integer; same seed + config + generator version reproduces the same town byte for byte.
nodes.impact: Re-rolls everything: the streets, households, weather, incidents and the year's draws. Use it to see how much results vary by chance alone.

nodes.title: Town
nodes.description: Override seed for geography only (roads growth, parcels, buildings).
nodes.impact: Re-rolls the geography (growth, lots, buildings). Households sit on lots, so they are drawn again too and usage totals shift by a few percent.

nodes.title: Households
nodes.description: Override seed for household attributes (occupants, solar, EV, heating).
nodes.impact: Re-rolls who lives where: occupants, solar, EVs, heating fuel, pools, payer profiles and tenancies. Streets stay put. Small towns move several percent on solar export.

nodes.title: Weather
nodes.description: Override seed for weather series (re-roll storms, keep the town).
nodes.impact: Re-rolls the daily temperatures: heating and cooling usage follow, and so do the cold days that make AMI, AMR and walked reads miss more often.

nodes.title: Incidents
nodes.description: Override seed for incident hazards.
nodes.impact: Re-rolls the random leaks, breaks, faults and collector outages, on the operations day and across the year, so the outage and gas odour contacts move too.

nodes.title: Anomalies
nodes.description: Override seed for the meter-to-cash run (missed reads, anomalies, analyst work, bill checks); a request's run seed overrides it per run.
nodes.impact: Re-rolls the year's draws (missed reads, anomalies, analyst work, bill checks) on the same households. A run's own seed overrides it without building a new town.

nodes.title: Houses
nodes.description: Number of residential premises to place.
nodes.impact: The number of homes. Accounts, reads, exceptions, bills and staffing load scale with it; a bigger town also spreads further, so its edge reaches newer eras.

nodes.title: Units
nodes.description: Display unit profile (stored values are always SI).
nodes.impact: How values are labelled (Ontario, US or UK units). Stored values stay SI; no result changes.

nodes.title: Anchor Lat
nodes.description: Latitude of the town (sun path, day length).
nodes.impact: Where the town sits on the globe: its latitude and the sun path in the map's day and night. Measured: no usage, network or year change.

nodes.title: Anchor Lon
nodes.description: Longitude of the town.
nodes.impact: Where the town sits on the globe (its longitude). Measured: no usage, network or year change.

nodes.title: Timezone
nodes.description: IANA timezone of the town (read schedules, billing calendar, day/night).
nodes.impact: The local clock for timestamps, read schedules and business days. Measured: the year's figures do not change, only the times printed on records.

nodes.title: Terrain Relief M
nodes.description: Peak-to-trough terrain relief.
nodes.impact: Hillier towns get a second water pressure zone, another elevated tank and PRVs or boosters at zone boundaries: pressures on the operations day.

nodes.title: Terrain Wavelength M
nodes.description: Dominant wavelength of terrain undulation.
nodes.impact: How quickly the ground rises and falls: elevations, water pressures and zone boundaries on the operations day.

nodes.title: Arterial Spacing M
nodes.description: Mean spacing of arterial roads (concession-grid style).
nodes.impact: Synthetic towns and grown districts only: how far apart the main roads run, so block sizes and drive times. On a real-street town it does nothing.

nodes.title: Arterial Warp M
nodes.description: Amplitude of the smooth warp applied to arterials.
nodes.impact: Synthetic towns and grown districts only: how much the main roads bend.

nodes.title: Collector Block M
nodes.description: Superblocks larger than this get a collector road.
nodes.impact: Synthetic towns and grown districts only: superblocks larger than this get a collector road.

nodes.title: Era Core Year
nodes.description: Construction year at the town centre.
nodes.impact: When the centre was built; ages every home. Older homes leak more heat (more gas or electric heating), rent more, have less solar and EV, and sit on overhead lines and cast-iron mains.

nodes.title: Era Span Years
nodes.description: Years added from centre to edge (era = core + span·(d/R)^1.2 + noise).
nodes.impact: How much newer the edge is than the centre. A wider span puts more homes in the modern era: better insulation, more solar, EVs, pools and irrigation.

nodes.title: Era Noise Years
nodes.description: Std-dev of era noise per district.
nodes.impact: Scatter of construction years between districts: a few districts change era, which shifts their insulation, appliances and tenure.

nodes.title: Park Share
nodes.description: Share of blocks kept as parks.
nodes.impact: Blocks kept as parks. Homes move to other blocks; the count stays the same.

nodes.title: Commercial Strip M
nodes.description: Length of the downtown main street: arterial frontage within half this distance of the centre is all commercial (up to 80 lots). The frontage shares below apply beyond it.
nodes.impact: Length of the all-commercial main street downtown: more storefront accounts with commercial usage, tariffs and gas heat.

nodes.title: Commercial Share Arterial
nodes.description: Share of developed lots fronting an arterial (beyond the downtown main street) that become commercial or mixed-use premises. The rest are homes, or rear yards where modern subdivisions back onto the arterial.
nodes.impact: Share of arterial frontage that becomes shops: more commercial accounts (large, steady electric and gas loads) while homes stay at the count.

nodes.title: Commercial Share Collector
nodes.description: Share of developed lots fronting a collector that become commercial or mixed-use premises.
nodes.impact: Share of collector frontage that becomes shops: more commercial accounts.

nodes.title: Commercial Share Local
nodes.description: Share of developed lots on local streets that become commercial (corner stores near downtown and where local streets meet main roads).
nodes.impact: Corner stores on local streets: a few more commercial accounts.

nodes.title: Commercial Cluster M
nodes.description: Distance over which commercial frontage clusters around main-road intersections and downtown. Smaller gives tight corner clusters, larger gives long strips.
nodes.impact: How tightly shops cluster around main-road junctions and downtown. Which lots hold shops changes, not how many.

nodes.title: Industrial Lots
nodes.description: Number of large industrial customers.
nodes.impact: Large industrial customers. Each is a very large electric, gas and water account; two of them are about a tenth of a small town's usage.

nodes.title: Houses Per School
nodes.description: One school per this many houses.
nodes.impact: One school per this many homes, rounded (towns under about 1,250 homes have none). A school is an institutional account with a large floor area, heavy water use and gas heat.

nodes.title: Margin M
nodes.description: Empty margin around the developed area.
nodes.impact: Empty land around the developed area, where utility sites sit. It moves things on the map only.

nodes.title: Corridor Max Deflection Deg
nodes.description: Arterial/collector road edges continue one corridor through a junction when the heading changes by at most this much.
nodes.impact: How sharp a bend still counts as one road corridor: feeder routes follow corridors, so it can change which customers share a feeder (and an outage) on the operations day.

nodes.title: Corridor Name Bonus Deg
nodes.description: Extra deflection allowed when both edges carry the same street name (a name is weak evidence of continuity).
nodes.impact: Extra bend allowed when both roads share a name, for feeder corridors on the operations day.

nodes.title: EraValues
nodes.description: Mean lot frontage by era.
nodes.impact: Wider lots build wider houses (55 to 70 percent of the frontage, up to 15 m): more floor area, so more heating and base load. Fewer lots fit each street, so homes spread to other streets and eras. Pools need lots over 600 m².

nodes.title: Pre 1945
nodes.impact: Wider lots build wider houses (55 to 70 percent of the frontage, up to 15 m): more floor area, so more heating and base load. Fewer lots fit each street, so homes spread to other streets and eras. Pools need lots over 600 m².

nodes.title: Postwar
nodes.impact: Wider lots build wider houses (55 to 70 percent of the frontage, up to 15 m): more floor area, so more heating and base load. Fewer lots fit each street, so homes spread to other streets and eras. Pools need lots over 600 m².

nodes.title: Modern
nodes.impact: Wider lots build wider houses (55 to 70 percent of the frontage, up to 15 m): more floor area, so more heating and base load. Fewer lots fit each street, so homes spread to other streets and eras. Pools need lots over 600 m².

nodes.title: EraValues
nodes.description: Mean lot depth by era.
nodes.impact: Deeper lots are larger (pools need over 600 m²) and leave room for deeper houses on shallow streets. On synthetic towns it also reshapes blocks, which re-draws households, so totals move by about seed-sized noise.

nodes.title: Pre 1945
nodes.impact: Deeper lots are larger (pools need over 600 m²) and leave room for deeper houses on shallow streets. On synthetic towns it also reshapes blocks, which re-draws households, so totals move by about seed-sized noise.

nodes.title: Postwar
nodes.impact: Deeper lots are larger (pools need over 600 m²) and leave room for deeper houses on shallow streets. On synthetic towns it also reshapes blocks, which re-draws households, so totals move by about seed-sized noise.

nodes.title: Modern
nodes.impact: Deeper lots are larger (pools need over 600 m²) and leave room for deeper houses on shallow streets. On synthetic towns it also reshapes blocks, which re-draws households, so totals move by about seed-sized noise.

nodes.title: EraValues
nodes.description: Front setback by era.
nodes.impact: How far houses sit back from the street. On shallow lots a deep setback makes the house shallower, a fraction of a percent of usage.

nodes.title: Pre 1945
nodes.impact: How far houses sit back from the street. On shallow lots a deep setback makes the house shallower, a fraction of a percent of usage.

nodes.title: Postwar
nodes.impact: How far houses sit back from the street. On shallow lots a deep setback makes the house shallower, a fraction of a percent of usage.

nodes.title: Modern
nodes.impact: How far houses sit back from the street. On shallow lots a deep setback makes the house shallower, a fraction of a percent of usage.

nodes.title: EraValues
nodes.description: Share of two-storey houses by era.
nodes.impact: Two storeys double the floor area on the same footprint: more heating in winter, more cooling and base load, and higher bills.

nodes.title: Pre 1945
nodes.impact: Two storeys double the floor area on the same footprint: more heating in winter, more cooling and base load, and higher bills.

nodes.title: Postwar
nodes.impact: Two storeys double the floor area on the same footprint: more heating in winter, more cooling and base load, and higher bills.

nodes.title: Modern
nodes.impact: Two storeys double the floor area on the same footprint: more heating in winter, more cooling and base load, and higher bills.

nodes.title: Occupancy Rate
nodes.description: Share of premises occupied at simulation start.
nodes.impact: Vacant homes use almost nothing (12 percent of base load, 3 percent of water). Fewer occupied homes: lower usage, more zero-use reads for VEE, vacant-consuming cases and first bills at move-in.

nodes.title: Rental Share
nodes.description: Share of premises that are rentals (more contract turnover).
nodes.impact: Rentals turn over: more move-ins and move-outs, so more first bills, final bills, short tenancies and contract changes for billing and collections.

nodes.title: Household Size Weights
nodes.description: Relative frequency of households with 1..6 occupants.
nodes.impact: Bigger households use more water (people times litres per day) and more base electricity: higher water bills above all.

nodes.title: EraValues
nodes.description: Share of houses with rooftop PV by era.
nodes.impact: Homes with rooftop PV by era: export registers, net-metering credits on bills, and low or negative summer net use that VEE and billing must handle.

nodes.title: Pre 1945
nodes.impact: Homes with rooftop PV by era: export registers, net-metering credits on bills, and low or negative summer net use that VEE and billing must handle.

nodes.title: Postwar
nodes.impact: Homes with rooftop PV by era: export registers, net-metering credits on bills, and low or negative summer net use that VEE and billing must handle.

nodes.title: Modern
nodes.impact: Homes with rooftop PV by era: export registers, net-metering credits on bills, and low or negative summer net use that VEE and billing must handle.

nodes.title: Pv Kw Min
nodes.description: Smallest rooftop PV system.
nodes.impact: Smallest PV system: more export and larger net-metering credits per solar home.

nodes.title: Pv Kw Max
nodes.description: Largest rooftop PV system.
nodes.impact: Largest PV system: more export and larger summer credits per solar home.

nodes.title: EraValues
nodes.description: Share of houses with an EV charger.
nodes.impact: EV chargers add about 6.5 kWh a day per home, all year: higher electric usage and bills, and bigger transformers on the map.

nodes.title: Pre 1945
nodes.impact: EV chargers add about 6.5 kWh a day per home, all year: higher electric usage and bills, and bigger transformers on the map.

nodes.title: Postwar
nodes.impact: EV chargers add about 6.5 kWh a day per home, all year: higher electric usage and bills, and bigger transformers on the map.

nodes.title: Modern
nodes.impact: EV chargers add about 6.5 kWh a day per home, all year: higher electric usage and bills, and bigger transformers on the map.

nodes.title: EraValues
nodes.description: Share of houses heated electrically (baseboard or heat pump) where gas is available. All houses in all-electric districts are electric.
nodes.impact: Electric instead of gas heat: winter electric usage and bills rise, gas accounts and gas usage fall.

nodes.title: Pre 1945
nodes.impact: Electric instead of gas heat: winter electric usage and bills rise, gas accounts and gas usage fall.

nodes.title: Postwar
nodes.impact: Electric instead of gas heat: winter electric usage and bills rise, gas accounts and gas usage fall.

nodes.title: Modern
nodes.impact: Electric instead of gas heat: winter electric usage and bills rise, gas accounts and gas usage fall.

nodes.title: Heat Pump Share Of Electric
nodes.description: Share of electric heating that is a heat pump (vs baseboard).
nodes.impact: Heat pumps use far less than baseboard heat for the same warmth: lower winter electric usage and bills.

nodes.title: Ac Rate
nodes.description: Share of houses with central air conditioning.
nodes.impact: Central air adds cooling load on hot days: higher July and August electric usage and bills, and summer high-bill checks.

nodes.title: Pool Rate
nodes.description: Share of houses (on lots > 600 m²) with a pool.
nodes.impact: Pools (only on lots over 600 m², more in modern districts) run a pump and heater on electricity, about 7.5 kWh a day from May to September, and top up 0.15 m³ of water a day. Pools are not heated with gas in this engine.

nodes.title: Irrigation Rate
nodes.description: Share of houses that irrigate lawns in summer.
nodes.impact: Lawn watering adds summer water use (May to September, peaking in July): higher summer water bills and seasonal swings VEE must accept.

nodes.title: Primary Kv
nodes.description: Primary distribution line-to-line voltage (Ontario urban 13.8 kV; US 12.47 kV).
nodes.impact: Feeder voltage: voltage drop and loading in the operations day's power flow.

nodes.title: Secondary V
nodes.description: Split-phase secondary voltage (120/240 V).
nodes.impact: Service voltage for the power flow and the voltage readings on the map.

nodes.title: Kva Per 100M2
nodes.description: Individual peak demand per 100 m² of floor area (lighting, plug, appliances).
nodes.impact: Design load per floor area: transformer and conductor sizes, so loading and overload failures on the operations day. Usage is not affected.

nodes.title: Kva Ac
nodes.description: Added peak for central air conditioning.
nodes.impact: Design load added for air conditioning: equipment sizing on the map.

nodes.title: Kva Electric Heat
nodes.description: Added peak for electric resistance heat.
nodes.impact: Design load added for electric heat: equipment sizing on the map.

nodes.title: Kva Heat Pump
nodes.description: Added peak for a heat pump.
nodes.impact: Design load added for a heat pump: equipment sizing on the map.

nodes.title: Kva Ev
nodes.description: Added peak for a Level-2 EV charger.
nodes.impact: Design load added for an EV charger: equipment sizing on the map.

nodes.title: Kva Pool
nodes.description: Added peak for a pool pump/heater.
nodes.impact: Design load added for a pool: equipment sizing on the map.

nodes.title: Coincidence Floor
nodes.description: Coincidence factor CF(n) = a + (1-a)/√n; a is the floor as n → ∞.
nodes.impact: How much peaks overlap: larger floors size bigger transformers and feeders.

nodes.title: Transformer Kva Steps
nodes.description: Single-phase transformer sizes.
nodes.impact: The transformer sizes available: groupings, loading and overloads on the map.

nodes.title: Transformer Max Loading
nodes.description: Allowed peak loading relative to nameplate.
nodes.impact: Allowed loading before a bigger transformer is chosen: overloaded units fail three times as often on the operations day.

nodes.title: Conductor Planning Margin
nodes.description: Primary conductors are sized for design load × this margin (winter peaks, load growth).
nodes.impact: Head-room in primary conductor sizing: thicker conductors, less loading on the map.

nodes.title: Max Houses Per Transformer Overhead
nodes.description: Max houses on a pole-mount transformer.
nodes.impact: Houses per pole transformer: how many customers lose power when one fails.

nodes.title: Max Houses Per Transformer Underground
nodes.description: Max houses on a pad-mount transformer.
nodes.impact: Houses per pad transformer: how many customers lose power when one fails.

nodes.title: Feeder Design Mva
nodes.description: Design peak per feeder.
nodes.impact: Design peak per feeder: how many feeders, and so how many customers one feeder fault interrupts.

nodes.title: Feeder Max Customers
nodes.description: Most customers planned on one feeder (limits how many lose supply when a feeder breaker trips).
nodes.impact: Most customers on one feeder: the largest outage one breaker trip can cause.

nodes.title: Min Feeders Per Substation
nodes.description: Feeders leaving each substation at least (fewer only when it serves fewer transformer groups), so normally-open ties can back-feed.
nodes.impact: Feeders per substation, so ties can back-feed during an outage.

nodes.title: Substation Mva
nodes.description: Firm capacity per substation.
nodes.impact: Firm capacity per substation: big towns get a second substation.

nodes.title: Route Weight Arterial
nodes.description: Feeder routing cost per metre along an arterial (trunks follow the cheapest corridors).
nodes.impact: Feeder routing cost along arterials: where trunks run and which customers share them.

nodes.title: Route Weight Collector
nodes.description: Feeder routing cost per metre along a collector.
nodes.impact: Feeder routing cost along collector roads: where trunks run on the map.

nodes.title: Route Weight Local
nodes.description: Feeder routing cost per metre along a local street.
nodes.impact: Feeder routing cost along local streets: where trunks run on the map.

nodes.title: Route Turn Penalty M
nodes.description: Routing cost of a 90° turn, in weighted metres; it grows with the square of the angle (a U-turn costs 4×). Bends under 10° are free.
nodes.impact: How much feeders avoid turns: straighter, longer trunks.

nodes.title: Route Corridor Change Penalty M
nodes.description: Routing cost of switching from one arterial/collector corridor to another.
nodes.impact: How much feeders avoid switching corridors: straighter feeders on the map.

nodes.title: Route Hierarchy Penalty M
nodes.description: Routing cost per step up or down the road hierarchy (arterial ↔ collector ↔ local).
nodes.impact: How much feeders avoid stepping between road classes.

nodes.title: Trunk Min Load Share
nodes.description: A feeder trunk extends along a corridor while at least this share of the feeder's connected load lies at or beyond that point; smaller tails are served by laterals.
nodes.impact: How far a three-phase trunk extends before laterals take over.

nodes.title: Route Shared Trunk Factor
nodes.description: Cost multiplier for running a feeder express through another feeder's territory or alongside its trunk.
nodes.impact: How much feeders avoid running through each other's territory.

nodes.title: Ties Per Feeder Pair
nodes.description: Normally-open tie switches between each pair of neighbouring feeders (0: no ties at all, section ties included).
nodes.impact: Normally-open ties: with ties, crews restore part of a faulted feeder from a neighbour, so outages are shorter on the operations day.

nodes.title: Tie Max Length M
nodes.description: Longest new line built for a tie: to a feeder that touches no other feeder, or from a switched section to another feeder's three-phase line (or round to its own feeder's). Along a street a line already uses, a metre counts 1.25 (single-phase) or 2 (three-phase).
nodes.impact: Longest line built for a tie: more ties, more restoration options.

nodes.title: Section Max Share
nodes.description: Sectionalising switches cut each feeder's three-phase backbone into sections of at most this share of the feeder's customers (at least section_min_customers), so a crew isolates a fault within a bounded section and ties back-feed the healthy sections beyond it.
nodes.impact: Sectionalising switches: smaller sections mean a fault takes out fewer customers.

nodes.title: Section Min Customers
nodes.description: Smallest section limit: a feeder is not cut into sections smaller than this many customers.
nodes.impact: Smallest section a feeder is cut into: how few customers one fault can take out.

nodes.title: Overhead Before Year
nodes.description: Districts built before this year are overhead (poles); later underground.
nodes.impact: Districts built before this year are on poles: storm faults and pole transformers on the operations day.

nodes.title: Pole Spacing M
nodes.description: Pole span on overhead lines.
nodes.impact: Pole span on overhead lines: pole count, and where AMI collectors can mount.

nodes.title: Voltage Min Pu
nodes.description: Lower service voltage limit (CSA CAN3-C235 / ANSI Range A). Frames report it on a 120 V base (premises.voltageLimits) with the premises below it; less 4 V it is the default floor for back-feeding through a tie.
nodes.impact: Low-voltage limit for the voltage readings on the map.

nodes.title: Voltage Max Pu
nodes.description: Upper service voltage limit (premises.voltageLimits in frames).
nodes.impact: High-voltage limit for the voltage readings on the map.

nodes.title: All Electric District Share
nodes.description: Share of districts with no gas mains (all-electric).
nodes.impact: Share of districts without gas mains, counted in whole districts, the core last (1: no gas mains at all): those homes heat with electricity, mostly heat pumps. Gas accounts and usage fall, winter electric usage rises. One-district towns (under 2,251 homes: village, small_town) have none whatever the share.

nodes.title: Scheme
nodes.description: Medium-pressure PE everywhere with a regulator at every meter, optionally with a legacy low-pressure core fed by district regulators.
nodes.impact: Medium pressure everywhere or a legacy low-pressure core: regulators and pressures on the map.

nodes.title: Transmission Kpa
nodes.description: Off-map transmission pressure at the city gate inlet.
nodes.impact: Pressure into the city gate: gas pressures on the operations day.

nodes.title: Mp Kpa
nodes.description: Medium-pressure distribution set point (60 psig).
nodes.impact: Medium-pressure set point: gas pressures on the operations day.

nodes.title: Lp Kpa
nodes.description: Low-pressure legacy main set point (7 in w.c.).
nodes.impact: Low-pressure core set point: gas pressures on the operations day.

nodes.title: Lp Core Before Year
nodes.description: Districts built before this year are on the low-pressure system.
nodes.impact: Districts older than this sit on the low-pressure core.

nodes.title: Design M3H Base
nodes.description: Design-hour demand per house, base component (≈ 40 CFH).
nodes.impact: Design-hour demand per house: gas main sizes. Usage is not affected.

nodes.title: Design M3H Per M2
nodes.description: Design-hour demand per m² of floor area (≈ 0.6 CFH/m²).
nodes.impact: Design-hour demand per floor area: gas main sizes.

nodes.title: Coincidence Floor
nodes.description: Gas coincidence factor floor a in CF(n) = a + (1-a)/√n.
nodes.impact: How much gas peaks overlap: larger floors size bigger gas mains.

nodes.title: Min Main Mm
nodes.description: Smallest distribution main (2-inch PE).
nodes.impact: Smallest gas main: pipe sizes and pressures on the map. Usage is not affected.

nodes.title: Valve Spacing M
nodes.description: Maximum spacing of main valves on feeders.
nodes.impact: Valve spacing: how much main a leak repair isolates.

nodes.title: Calorific Mj Per M3
nodes.description: Higher heating value used for energy conversion (therm/kWh display and billing).
nodes.impact: Energy per cubic metre for showing gas in GJ or therms. Bills charge per m³, so no amount changes.

nodes.title: Base Pressure Kpa
nodes.description: Base pressure for standard volume: the Weymouth base pressure in gas main sizing and pressures (default 14.73 psia).
nodes.impact: Standard-volume base pressure in the gas flow equations.

nodes.title: Base Temperature C
nodes.description: Base temperature for standard volume: the Weymouth base temperature (default 520 °R, about 60 °F).
nodes.impact: Standard-volume base temperature in the gas flow equations.

nodes.title: Lpcd
nodes.description: Indoor residential use per person per day.
nodes.impact: Indoor water per person per day: every home's water usage and bill scales with it, and wastewater charges follow.

nodes.title: Irrigation M3 Per Day
nodes.description: Summer irrigation per irrigating house.
nodes.impact: Summer watering per irrigating home: higher summer water usage and bills.

nodes.title: Max Day Factor
nodes.description: Max-day / average-day ratio.
nodes.impact: Max-day demand used to size mains and storage on the map.

nodes.title: Peak Hour Factor
nodes.description: Peak-hour / average-day ratio.
nodes.impact: Peak-hour demand used to size mains: pipe sizes and pressures on the map.

nodes.title: Fire Flow Residential Lps
nodes.description: Required residential fire flow (1,000 USgpm).
nodes.impact: Fire flow that sizes residential mains: bigger mains, lower velocities.

nodes.title: Fire Flow Commercial Lps
nodes.description: Required commercial/institutional fire flow.
nodes.impact: Fire flow that sizes commercial mains: pipe sizes and pressures on the map.

nodes.title: Fire Flow Industrial Lps
nodes.description: Required industrial fire flow.
nodes.impact: Fire flow that sizes the industrial and supply mains.

nodes.title: Min Main Mm
nodes.description: Smallest main where hydrants are attached.
nodes.impact: Smallest main that carries hydrants: pipe sizes and pressures on the map.

nodes.title: Collector Main Mm
nodes.description: Minimum main on collector roads.
nodes.impact: Smallest main on collector roads: pipe sizes and pressures on the map.

nodes.title: Arterial Main Mm
nodes.description: Minimum transmission main on arterials leaving the pump station.
nodes.impact: Smallest transmission main from the pump station.

nodes.title: Hw C New
nodes.description: Hazen-Williams C for PVC/ductile iron mains.
nodes.impact: Pipe roughness of new mains: pressures on the operations day.

nodes.title: Hw C Old
nodes.description: Hazen-Williams C for unlined cast iron mains.
nodes.impact: Pipe roughness of old cast iron: more head loss, lower pressures.

nodes.title: Cast Iron Before Year
nodes.description: Mains along streets built before this year are unlined cast iron (the concrete trunk excepted).
nodes.impact: Mains older than this are cast iron: rougher and break twice as often on the operations day.

nodes.title: Tank Overflow Above Ground M
nodes.description: Elevated tank overflow height above the highest service in its zone.
nodes.impact: Elevated tank height: static pressure in its zone.

nodes.title: Zone Band M
nodes.description: Elevation band per pressure zone.
nodes.impact: Elevation band per pressure zone: how many zones a hilly town needs.

nodes.title: Hydrant Spacing M
nodes.description: Hydrant spacing on residential mains.
nodes.impact: Hydrant spacing on residential mains: hydrant count on the map.

nodes.title: Hydrant Spacing Commercial M
nodes.description: Hydrant spacing in commercial areas.
nodes.impact: Hydrant spacing in commercial areas: hydrant count on the map.

nodes.title: Valve Spacing M
nodes.description: Maximum spacing between line valves.
nodes.impact: Valve spacing: how many customers a main break isolates.

nodes.title: Pump Units
nodes.description: Pumps at the booster station (one is standby).
nodes.impact: Pumps at the station, one on standby: pumping capacity on the operations day.

nodes.title: Ami Route Share
nodes.description: Share of meter reading routes converted to AMI.
nodes.impact: Routes read by AMI. AMI reads are cheapest and miss least (1.2 percent); moving routes to AMR or walkers raises read cost, missed reads, estimates and the work they create.

nodes.title: Amr Route Share
nodes.description: Share of routes read by drive-by AMR vans (rest are walked manually).
nodes.impact: Routes read by drive-by AMR vans: costlier than AMI and missed more often (3 percent), with their own anomaly factor. The rest are walked.

nodes.title: Collector Radius M
nodes.description: AMI collector coverage radius.
nodes.impact: AMI collector reach: how many collectors, and how many meters go dark when one fails on the operations day.

nodes.title: Poll Start Hour
nodes.description: Nightly head-end poll window start (local time).
nodes.impact: When the nightly AMI poll starts: the time stamped on AMI reads. Results do not change.

nodes.title: Poll End Hour
nodes.description: Nightly head-end poll window end.
nodes.impact: When the nightly AMI poll ends: the latest time stamped on AMI reads. Results do not change.

nodes.title: Meter Digits Electric
nodes.description: Register digits on electric meters (rollover at 10^digits).
nodes.impact: Register digits on electric meters: where registers roll over, and how far a transposed or misread digit throws a read.

nodes.title: Meter Digits Water
nodes.description: Register digits on water meters.
nodes.impact: Register digits on water meters: rollover and digit-error size.

nodes.title: Meter Digits Gas
nodes.description: Register digits on gas meters.
nodes.impact: Register digits on gas meters: rollover and digit-error size.

nodes.title: SeasonTemp
nodes.description: Winter (Dec 21–Mar 20).
nodes.impact: Winter temperatures: colder winters raise heating usage (gas, or electricity for electric homes), winter bills, and the deep-cold days below -10 °C when reads miss more.

nodes.impact: Winter temperatures: colder winters raise heating usage (gas, or electricity for electric homes), winter bills, and the deep-cold days below -10 °C when reads miss more.

nodes.title: Sd C
nodes.impact: Winter temperatures: colder winters raise heating usage (gas, or electricity for electric homes), winter bills, and the deep-cold days below -10 °C when reads miss more.

nodes.title: Min C
nodes.impact: Winter temperatures: colder winters raise heating usage (gas, or electricity for electric homes), winter bills, and the deep-cold days below -10 °C when reads miss more.

nodes.title: Max C
nodes.impact: Winter temperatures: colder winters raise heating usage (gas, or electricity for electric homes), winter bills, and the deep-cold days below -10 °C when reads miss more.

nodes.impact: Spring temperatures: a cold spring keeps heating usage and bills up into April and May.

nodes.impact: Spring temperatures: a cold spring keeps heating usage and bills up into April and May.

nodes.impact: Summer temperatures: hotter summers raise cooling usage and bills on homes with air conditioning.

nodes.impact: Fall temperatures: an early cold snap raises October and November heating usage and bills.

nodes.title: Persistence
nodes.description: Day-to-day AR(1) persistence of temperature anomalies.
nodes.impact: How long warm or cold spells last: longer spells make monthly usage swing more from normal, which VEE's tolerances see.

nodes.title: Storm Days Per Year
nodes.description: Thunderstorm days per year (mostly May–Sep).
nodes.impact: Thunderstorm days: overhead faults and outages on the operations day and across the year, with the outage reports they bring to the contact centre.

nodes.title: Heating Base C
nodes.description: Heating starts below this temperature.
nodes.impact: Heating starts below this temperature: a higher base means more heating usage in spring and fall.

nodes.title: Cooling Base C
nodes.description: Cooling starts above this temperature.
nodes.impact: Cooling starts above this temperature: a lower base means more cooling usage.

nodes.title: Gas Service Leaks Per 1000
nodes.description: Leaks per 1,000 gas services per year.
nodes.impact: Random service leaks on the operations day and across the year: gas odour calls and a household without gas until the repair.

nodes.title: Gas Main Leaks Per 100Km
nodes.description: Leaks per 100 km of gas main per year.
nodes.impact: Random gas main leaks on the operations day and across the year: crew calls, isolations and gas odour calls from the neighbours.

nodes.title: Water Main Breaks Per 100Km
nodes.description: Main breaks per 100 km per year (×2 for cast iron).
nodes.impact: Random main breaks on the operations day and across the year: customers without water and the outage reports they make.

nodes.title: Overhead Faults Per Km Storm Day
nodes.description: Overhead primary faults per km per storm day.
nodes.impact: Storm faults on overhead lines: feeder outages on storm days, on the operations day and across the year, and the outage reports.

nodes.title: Transformer Failures Per 1000
nodes.description: Transformer failures per 1,000 units per year (×3 when overloaded).
nodes.impact: Transformer failures (three times as many where units are overloaded): small outages on the operations day and across the year.

nodes.title: Collector Outages Per Year
nodes.description: AMI collector outages per year (town-wide).
nodes.impact: AMI collector outages: the meters behind it miss their nightly read that day. Customers do not notice them.

nodes.title: Manual Only
nodes.description: Disable random hazards; only manually injected incidents occur (the run's "Random incidents" switch defaults to the opposite).
nodes.impact: Turns random incidents off on the operations day; only the ones you inject happen. The year draws them unless Outages & leaks is off.

nodes.title: Gas Crews
nodes.description: Gas emergency crews.
nodes.impact: Gas crews: how fast leaks are made safe on the operations day.

nodes.title: Electric Crews
nodes.description: Electric trouble crews.
nodes.impact: Electric crews: how long outages last on the operations day.

nodes.title: Water Crews
nodes.description: Water distribution crews.
nodes.impact: Water crews: how long main breaks keep customers off.

nodes.title: Meter Techs
nodes.description: Meter technicians (exchanges, investigations).
nodes.impact: Meter technicians for exchanges and investigations on the operations day. The year's field capacity is Field orders per day.

nodes.title: Meter Vans
nodes.description: Drive-by AMR reading vans.
nodes.impact: AMR vans driving routes on the operations day; routes are shared among them.

nodes.title: Meter Walkers
nodes.description: Manual meter readers.
nodes.impact: Walkers reading manual routes on the operations day.

nodes.title: Shift Start Hour
nodes.description: Day shift start. Non-emergency work (AMI collector repairs) waits for the day shift; emergencies are worked around the clock.
nodes.impact: When the day shift starts: non-emergency repairs wait for it.

nodes.title: Shift End Hour
nodes.description: Day shift end.
nodes.impact: When the day shift ends: non-emergency repairs left after it wait for the next morning.

nodes.title: Gas Response Target Min
nodes.description: Target response to a gas odour call.
nodes.impact: The response target gas crews are measured against on the operations day.

nodes.title: Speed Kmh Arterial
nodes.description: Driving speed on arterials.
nodes.impact: Driving speed on arterials: crew and van travel times.

nodes.title: Speed Kmh Collector
nodes.description: Driving speed on collectors.
nodes.impact: Driving speed on collector roads: crew and van travel times on the operations day.

nodes.title: Speed Kmh Local
nodes.description: Driving speed on local streets.
nodes.impact: Driving speed on local streets: crew and van travel times on the operations day.

nodes.title: Services
nodes.description: The services your utility provides in this town. The networks are there either way; for a service you do not provide, another utility runs it: no accounts, meters, reads, bills, crews, maintenance or calls of yours, and its settings do not apply.
nodes.impact: The services your utility provides here. For a service it does not provide, another utility runs the network: no accounts, meters, reads, bills, crews, maintenance, incidents or calls of yours, and its settings do not apply. A new town (the networks are the same; the customers change).

nodes.title: Mru Target Meters
nodes.description: Target premises per meter reading unit (route).
nodes.impact: Premises per reading route. Every town gets at least one route per billing portion (21), so it only bites above about 9,500 premises; then smaller routes mean more of them and a different split of AMI, AMR and walked routes.

nodes.title: Bill Cycles
nodes.description: Billing portions per month (one per working day).
nodes.impact: Billing portions per month: how reads and bills spread across working days, so daily queue load and when bills go out.

nodes.title: Currency
nodes.description: Billing currency.
nodes.impact: The currency label on bills. Amounts do not change.

nodes.title: Tax Rate
nodes.description: Sales tax on utility bills (Ontario HST).
nodes.impact: Sales tax on every bill: invoice totals, receivables and late fees scale with it.

nodes.title: Electric Fixed Monthly
nodes.description: Electric fixed delivery charge per month.
nodes.impact: Fixed electric charge: every electric bill moves by this, whatever the usage.

nodes.title: Electric Blocks
nodes.description: Electric energy price blocks per kWh (summer threshold).
nodes.impact: Energy price blocks: bill amounts, high-bill checks and the cost of each billing error.

nodes.title: Electric Variable Delivery
nodes.description: Electric variable delivery per kWh.
nodes.impact: Delivery charge per kWh: electric bills scale with usage.

nodes.title: Net Metering Credit
nodes.description: Credit per exported kWh.
nodes.impact: Credit per exported kWh: solar homes' summer bills and the large-credit checks.

nodes.title: Gas Fixed Monthly
nodes.description: Gas customer charge per month.
nodes.impact: Fixed gas charge: every gas bill moves by this, whatever the usage.

nodes.title: Gas Price M3
nodes.description: Gas delivery + supply per m³.
nodes.impact: Gas price per m³: winter gas bills scale with it.

nodes.title: Water Fixed Monthly
nodes.description: Water fixed charge per month.
nodes.impact: Fixed water charge: every water bill moves by this, whatever the usage.

nodes.title: Water Price M3
nodes.description: Water volumetric charge.
nodes.impact: Water price per m³: water bills scale with it, and wastewater follows it.

nodes.title: Wastewater Ratio
nodes.description: Wastewater charge as a multiple of the water volumetric charge.
nodes.impact: Wastewater as a multiple of the water price: water bills scale with it.

nodes.title: On Time Payer Share
nodes.description: Share of accounts that pay on time.
nodes.impact: Accounts that pay on time. Fewer means more overdue balances, reminders, notices, late fees and collections work.

nodes.title: Late Payer Share
nodes.description: Share that pay late.
nodes.impact: Accounts that pay late; the rest are at-risk payers who may not pay at all. More late and at-risk payers drive dunning and disconnections.

nodes.title: Pre Authorized Share
nodes.description: Share on pre-authorized debit.
nodes.impact: Accounts on pre-authorized debit: they pay on the due date, but a share bounce, which opens payment-rejected cases and NSF fees.

nodes.title: Due Days
nodes.description: Days from invoice to due date.
nodes.impact: Days from invoice to due date: when accounts go overdue, so receivable carry and the dunning calendar.

nodes.title: Rpa Coverage
nodes.description: Share of exception types with an RPA/auto-resolve rule.
nodes.impact: Share of exception types automation resolves. More coverage: fewer cases for analysts, cheaper and faster resolution, less carry; uncovered types still queue for people.

nodes.title: Analyst Queue Days Min
nodes.description: Minimum queue wait before an analyst picks up an exception.
nodes.impact: Shortest wait before an analyst first looks at a case: every human case takes at least this long, so carry and days to release rise.

nodes.title: Analyst Queue Days Max
nodes.description: Maximum queue wait.
nodes.impact: Longest first-look wait: the tail of slow cases, open-case counts and carry.

nodes.title: Carry Rate Per Day
nodes.description: Carrying cost per account per day before invoicing.
nodes.impact: Cost of a day a bill is held back. Prices the carry; it does not change which cases happen.

nodes.title: Receivable Carry Ratio
nodes.description: Receivable carry as a share of the billing carry rate.
nodes.impact: Carry on unpaid invoices as a share of the billing carry rate. Prices receivable carry only.

nodes.title: Analysts
nodes.description: Billing analysts working the exception queues.
nodes.impact: People working the queues. Fewer: backlog grows, cases age, estimates and blocked bills wait longer and carry builds; more: queues clear faster.

nodes.title: Analyst Hours Per Day
nodes.description: Productive queue hours per analyst per business day.
nodes.impact: Queue hours per analyst per day: capacity, like the number of analysts.

nodes.title: Review Minutes Min
nodes.description: Shortest analyst review.
nodes.impact: Shortest review: longer reviews cut how many cases a day each analyst clears.

nodes.title: Review Minutes Max
nodes.description: Longest analyst review.
nodes.impact: Longest review: capacity and labor cost per case.

nodes.title: Supervisors
nodes.description: Supervisors approving escalations.
nodes.impact: Supervisors approving escalations. Zero: escalated cases wait, high-impact bills stay held.

nodes.title: Supervisor Hours Per Day
nodes.description: Supervisor hours on escalations per business day.
nodes.impact: Supervisor time for escalations: how fast the Escalations queue clears.

nodes.title: Supervisor Minutes
nodes.description: Supervisor review time per escalation.
nodes.impact: Supervisor time per escalation: capacity and labor cost.

nodes.title: Supervisor Queue Days Min
nodes.description: Minimum wait before a supervisor picks up an escalation (VEE's own escalations wait this long).
nodes.impact: Shortest wait for a supervisor: escalated cases take at least this long.

nodes.title: Supervisor Queue Days Max
nodes.description: Maximum wait before a supervisor picks up an escalation from an analyst or you. An escalation you take yourself (assign) waits for you.
nodes.impact: Longest wait before a supervisor picks up an escalation: the tail of held high-impact bills.

nodes.title: Field Orders Per Day
nodes.description: Meter investigations, re-reads and exchanges completed per business day.
nodes.impact: Field orders worked per day (re-reads, checks, exchanges). Fewer: field backlog, longer estimate streaks, stuck and slow meters fixed later.

nodes.title: Field Days Min
nodes.description: Earliest a field order is worked after it is raised.
nodes.impact: Earliest a field order is worked after it is raised.

nodes.title: Analyst Accuracy
nodes.description: Share of reviews where the analyst finds the true cause.
nodes.impact: Reviews where the analyst finds the true cause. Lower: wrong dispositions, billing errors that surface later as rebills and complaints.

nodes.title: Enabled
nodes.description: Inject anomalies into observed reads (truth is always kept separately).
nodes.impact: Off: reads are clean apart from missed reads, so VEE flags only what usage swings and outages explain. Truth is always kept for scoring.

nodes.title: Leak
nodes.description: Continuous post-meter water leaks.
nodes.impact: Water leaks after the meter: high water reads, high-bill blocks and complaints.

nodes.title: Stuck Meter
nodes.description: Registers that stop advancing.
nodes.impact: Registers that stop: zero-use reads at occupied homes, field orders and exchanges, under-billing until fixed.

nodes.title: Slow Meter
nodes.description: Meters under-registering 10–40%.
nodes.impact: Meters under-registering 10 to 40 percent: lost revenue VEE catches only through the trend test.

nodes.title: Transposed Digits
nodes.description: Reads with two digits swapped.
nodes.impact: Two digits swapped in a read: wild spikes or drops VEE should reject.

nodes.title: Misread
nodes.description: Reads off by one in a high digit.
nodes.impact: A high digit off by one: large spikes or negative use.

nodes.title: Consecutive Estimates
nodes.description: Runs of 2–4 estimated periods (higher on manual routes).
nodes.impact: Runs of estimated periods (more on walked routes): estimate streaks that trigger field reads and true-ups.

nodes.title: Missing Read
nodes.description: Periods with no read document.
nodes.impact: Periods with no read document: estimates and missing-read cases.

nodes.title: Exchange Registration Failure
nodes.description: Meter exchanges whose new serial fails registration.
nodes.impact: Meter exchanges whose new meter fails registration: zero use, blocked bills and analyst or field work.

nodes.title: Vacant Consuming
nodes.description: Vacant premises that still consume.
nodes.impact: Vacant homes that still use energy: unbilled consumption cases.

nodes.title: Tamper
nodes.description: Bypass/tamper (50–90% under-registration).
nodes.impact: Bypasses that under-register 50 to 90 percent: lost revenue and investigations.

nodes.title: Amr Factor
nodes.description: Multiplier on every anomaly rate for AMR (drive-by) meters: an ageing ERT fleet misreads and under-registers more.
nodes.impact: Multiplies every anomaly rate on AMR meters: an ageing drive-by fleet misreads and under-registers more.

nodes.title: Manual Factor
nodes.description: Multiplier on every anomaly rate for manually read meters.
nodes.impact: Multiplies every anomaly rate on walked meters: more misreads and faults on manual routes.

nodes.title: Name
nodes.description: Live demonstration scenario.
nodes.impact: The map's demonstration (normal, solar noon, leak, substation outage) on the live day. The year is unchanged.

nodes.title: Date
nodes.description: Demonstration date (local).
nodes.impact: The day the map shows and the Studio opens on. The year's results are the same; only the default view date moves.

nodes.title: Hour
nodes.description: Demonstration hour (local, decimal).
nodes.impact: The hour the map's live clock starts at. The year is unchanged.

nodes.title: Target Premise
nodes.description: Premise targeted by the leak scenario (default: first premise).
nodes.impact: The premise the map's leak demonstration targets.

nodes.title: Leak M3H
nodes.description: Leak rate added to the target premise's water demand.
nodes.impact: Leak size in the map's leak demonstration: flows and pressures that day.

nodes.title: Ami Missed Read
nodes.description: AMI billing reads still missing after the head-end retry window (1: a day the head end is down).
nodes.impact: AMI reads still missing after retries: estimates, missing-read cases and estimate streaks.

nodes.title: Amr Missed Read
nodes.description: Drive-by reads missed (no signal, street skipped; 1: the van does not go out).
nodes.impact: Drive-by reads missed: estimates and missing-read cases on AMR routes.

nodes.title: Manual No Access
nodes.description: Manual reads with no access (locked gate, dog, meter inside; 1: nobody walks the route).
nodes.impact: Walked reads with no access: estimates, streaks and field reads.

nodes.title: No Access Repeat
nodes.description: Chance a missed manual read is missed again the next month.
nodes.impact: Chance a no-access meter is missed again next month: longer estimate streaks and more field reads.

nodes.title: Read Cost Ami
nodes.description: Cost of one AMI read.
nodes.impact: Cost of one AMI read. Prices reading; no read changes.

nodes.title: Read Cost Amr
nodes.description: Cost of one drive-by read.
nodes.impact: Cost of one drive-by read. Prices reading in the cost totals; no read changes.

nodes.title: Read Cost Manual
nodes.description: Cost of one walked read.
nodes.impact: Cost of one walked read. Prices reading in the cost totals; no read changes.

nodes.title: High Ratio
nodes.description: Flag consumption above this multiple of expected (tolerance high).
nodes.impact: Flag use above this multiple of expected. Lower: more high reads flagged (more cases, more real spikes caught, more false alarms).

nodes.title: Low Ratio
nodes.description: Flag consumption below this share of expected (tolerance low).
nodes.impact: Flag use below this share of expected. Higher: more low reads flagged, catching slow and stuck meters sooner at the cost of more cases.

nodes.title: Zero At Occupied
nodes.description: Flag zero consumption at an occupied premise.
nodes.impact: Flag zero use at an occupied home: catches stuck meters and failed exchanges.

nodes.title: Max Consecutive Estimates
nodes.description: Estimates in a row before a field read is ordered.
nodes.impact: Estimates in a row before a field read is ordered: lower means more field orders, shorter streaks.

nodes.title: Min Period Days
nodes.description: Shortest plausible read period.
nodes.impact: Shortest plausible read period: shorter periods fail the timing test.

nodes.title: Max Period Days
nodes.description: Longest plausible read period.
nodes.impact: Longest plausible read period: longer periods fail the timing test and go to review.

nodes.title: Accept Confidence
nodes.description: Auto-accept at or above this confidence.
nodes.impact: Auto-accept at or above this confidence. Higher: fewer reads auto-accepted, more for review.

nodes.title: Reject Confidence
nodes.description: Reject below this confidence.
nodes.impact: Reject below this confidence (the read is replaced by an estimate).

nodes.title: Escalate Impact
nodes.description: Escalate a doubtful read when its bill impact exceeds this.
nodes.impact: Doubtful reads whose bill impact exceeds this go to a supervisor: lower means more escalations and supervisor load.

nodes.title: Trend Ratio
nodes.description: Persistent low use: flag reads below this share of expected …
nodes.impact: Persistent low use below this share of expected is flagged: how slow meters and tamper are caught.

nodes.title: Trend Periods
nodes.description: … for this many periods in a row.
nodes.impact: Periods of low use before the trend flag: fewer means earlier detection, more cases.

nodes.title: Oms Events
nodes.description: Use outage events (OMS, AMI last gasps) from operations: hours without service lower the expected use.
nodes.impact: Use outage events: hours without service lower the expected use, so outage-explained low reads are accepted instead of flagged. Only matters when a run carries interruptions from an operations day.

nodes.title: Estimation
nodes.description: Estimation method for missing or rejected reads.
nodes.impact: How missing or rejected reads are estimated: prior year or average daily use. Changes estimated amounts and later true-ups.

nodes.title: History Noise
nodes.description: Spread of prior-year history around this year's normal usage.
nodes.impact: How far last year's history strays from this year's normal use: more noise, more reads look odd against history.

nodes.title: Rate Change Date
nodes.description: Date a new tariff version takes effect (volumetric prices).
nodes.impact: When the new tariff version starts: bills after it prorate across the change.

nodes.title: Rate Change Pct
nodes.description: Volumetric price change in the new tariff version.
nodes.impact: Price change in the new tariff version: bill amounts after the date.

nodes.title: High Bill Ratio
nodes.description: Block a bill above this multiple of its expected amount (prior-year use at current prices).
nodes.impact: Block bills above this multiple of expected: lower means more billing outsorts for analysts or RPA.

nodes.title: High Bill Min
nodes.description: …and at least this much above the expected amount.
nodes.impact: And at least this much above expected: filters small bills out of high-bill checks.

nodes.title: First Bill Limit
nodes.description: Block a bill with no expected use (vacant, new) above this total.
nodes.impact: Block first bills above this total when there is no expected use to compare with (vacant or new premises). Rare in small towns.

nodes.title: Credit Review
nodes.description: Block a bill that is a credit larger than this.
nodes.impact: Block credit bills larger than this for review: lower means more credit outsorts.

nodes.title: Outsort Auto Release Max
nodes.description: RPA may release a high-bill or large-credit outsort only up to this bill amount (either sign); a larger one waits for an analyst.
nodes.impact: RPA may release outsorts up to this amount; larger ones wait for an analyst.

nodes.title: Billing Queue Worked By
nodes.description: Who works the BILLING queue (high bills, large credits, true-ups, rate-class errors): the simulated analysts and RPA, or only you. With 'you', no analyst or RPA touches a billing block, so every outsort waits in the Studio for your release, rebill or escalation.
nodes.impact: Who works the Billing queue: analysts and RPA, or only you (cases wait for your decisions).

nodes.title: Trueup Max Ratio
nodes.description: Block a bill whose estimate true-up (a negative period quantity) is larger than this multiple of the period's expected use; an analyst decides it.
nodes.impact: Block estimate true-ups (a negative period after an over-estimate) larger than this multiple of expected use. Rare unless estimates run high.

nodes.title: Data Error Rate
nodes.description: Installations with a wrong rate class in billing master data (per 1,000 per year).
nodes.impact: Wrong rate classes in billing master data: mis-billed accounts, rate-class blocks and rebills.

nodes.title: Print Lag Days
nodes.description: Days from invoice creation to issue.
nodes.impact: Days from invoice to issue: due dates and receivable carry move with it.

nodes.title: Pad Reject Rate
nodes.description: Pre-authorized debits returned for insufficient funds.
nodes.impact: Pre-authorized debits that bounce: payment-rejected cases, NSF fees and overdue balances.

nodes.title: Nsf Fee
nodes.description: Fee for a returned payment.
nodes.impact: Fee added to an account when a payment bounces: higher balances and more overdue amounts.

nodes.title: Late Fee Pct
nodes.description: Late payment charge on overdue amounts (per notice).
nodes.impact: Late charge on overdue amounts at each notice: higher balances and receivables.

nodes.title: Reminder Days
nodes.description: Days after the due date for a reminder.
nodes.impact: Days after the due date for a reminder letter: when collections work starts.

nodes.title: Notice Days
nodes.description: Days after the due date for an overdue notice and late fee.
nodes.impact: Days after the due date for an overdue notice and late fee: when fees start to build.

nodes.title: Disconnect Days
nodes.description: Days after the due date for a disconnection notice.
nodes.impact: Days after the due date for a disconnection notice: later notices, fewer disconnections in the year.

nodes.title: Winter Moratorium
nodes.description: No disconnection notices for electricity and water from Nov 15 to Apr 30 (Ontario); a notice held for the winter is issued on May 1 if the bill is still unpaid.
nodes.impact: No electric or water disconnection notices in winter; held notices go out after the end date. Shifts collections from winter to spring.

nodes.title: Moratorium Start
nodes.description: First day of the winter moratorium (MM-DD).
nodes.impact: First day of the winter moratorium: an earlier start holds more autumn notices.

nodes.title: Moratorium End
nodes.description: Last day of the winter moratorium (MM-DD); held notices go out the day after.
nodes.impact: Last day of the winter moratorium; held notices go out the next day.

nodes.title: Disconnect Notice Days
nodes.description: Days from a disconnection notice to the earliest disconnection. A disconnection also needs a person's approval (the Collections worklist).
nodes.impact: Days from a disconnection notice to the earliest disconnection. Acts only on disconnections you approve: the engine never disconnects on its own.

nodes.title: Disconnect Rule Share
nodes.description: Share of disconnection notices a collections rule approves when they are issued (the disconnection follows at the earliest day); the rest wait for a person's approval. 0: every disconnection needs you.
nodes.impact: Disconnection notices a collections rule approves as they are issued: the crews' disconnects and reconnects follow, disconnected meters are not read or billed until reconnected, and disconnected contacts come in. 0 (the default): every disconnection waits for you.

nodes.title: Disconnect Payment Rate
nodes.description: Disconnected customers who pay within a week of the disconnection (and are reconnected the next business day); the rest stay off until they pay.
nodes.impact: Disconnected customers who pay within a week and are reconnected the next business day. Acts only on disconnections you approve in the Collections worklist.

nodes.title: Arrangement Break Rate
nodes.description: At-risk payers who break a payment arrangement after a few instalments (dunning resumes); other payers pay every instalment.
nodes.impact: At-risk payers who break a payment arrangement after a few instalments; dunning resumes. Acts only on arrangements you set up in the Collections worklist.

nodes.title: Low Income Referral Rate
nodes.description: Disconnection notices and winter moratorium holds after which the call centre refers the customer to a low-income programme (once a year per account).
nodes.impact: Notices and holds after which the customer is referred to a low-income programme; dunning waits.

nodes.title: Low Income Review Days
nodes.description: Business days the low-income agency takes to decide a referral; dunning waits meanwhile.
nodes.impact: Business days the agency takes to decide a referral; dunning waits meanwhile.

nodes.title: Low Income Approval Rate
nodes.description: Referrals the agency approves with a grant.
nodes.impact: Referrals approved with a grant against arrears: less owed, fewer disconnections.

nodes.title: Low Income Grant Max
nodes.description: Largest low-income grant credited to an account's arrears.
nodes.impact: Largest low-income grant credited to an account's arrears: less owed, fewer notices.

nodes.title: Budget Billing Offer Rate
nodes.description: Overdue notices after which the call centre enrols the customer in budget billing (once a year per account); the plan levels later invoices.
nodes.impact: Overdue notices after which the customer moves to budget billing: levelled later invoices.

nodes.title: Agents
nodes.description: Agents on the phones on a business day (a small utility often has one, shared with billing).
nodes.impact: Agents answering during opening hours. Fewer: longer waits, more hang-ups, call backs and repeat calls, and customers who give up pay later (more overdue bills); fewer disputes get through to become cases. More: shorter waits but more idle time and cost.

nodes.title: Open Hour
nodes.description: Lines open (local time, business days).
nodes.impact: When the lines open on business days. Later opening squeezes the same contacts into fewer hours: longer waits at peaks.

nodes.title: Close Hour
nodes.description: Lines close (local time).
nodes.impact: When the lines close. Earlier closing squeezes contacts into fewer hours; callers who find the lines closed try again the next day.

nodes.title: Patience
nodes.description: Average time a caller waits before hanging up.
nodes.impact: How long callers hold before hanging up. Less patience: more hang-ups and retries at the same waits, and more customers who pay later after bad service.

nodes.title: Retry Share
nodes.description: Callers who hung up or found the lines closed and try again.
nodes.impact: Callers who hung up or found the lines closed and try again: retries add load at busy times; the rest give up unanswered.

nodes.title: Repeat Share
nodes.description: Callers whose problem was not resolved who contact again within days.
nodes.impact: Customers whose problem was not resolved who contact again: repeat contacts, and complaints after a second failure.

nodes.title: Callback
nodes.description: Offer a call back instead of holding when the wait is long.
nodes.impact: Offer a call back instead of holding when the wait is long: fewer hang-ups, the same agent time spread later in the day.

nodes.title: Call back after
nodes.description: Offer the call back when the expected wait exceeds this.
nodes.impact: Expected wait at which the call back is offered: lower offers it more often, turning hang-ups into later calls.

nodes.title: Callback Take Share

nodes.impact: Callers who accept the call back offer.

nodes.title: Service target
nodes.description: Answer target for the service level (answered within it).
nodes.impact: The answer target the service level counts against. It changes the reported service level, not who waits.

nodes.title: Volume Factor
nodes.description: Multiplies every reason's contact rates.
nodes.impact: Multiplies every reason's rates: a quick way to test a busier or quieter year.

nodes.title: Handle Factor
nodes.description: Multiplies every reason's handling time.
nodes.impact: Multiplies every handling time: slower handling fills the agents' day, so waits and hang-ups rise, and frustrated customers pay later.

nodes.title: Self Serve Factor
nodes.description: Multiplies every reason's self-service share (0: IVR and web down).
nodes.impact: Multiplies the share the IVR and website handle; zero sends every contact to an agent.

nodes.title: Agent Cost Per Hour

nodes.impact: Prices the agents' open hours in the contact cost. No contact changes.

nodes.title: Dispute Cases
nodes.description: Share of answered bill-wrong contacts (and unresolved high-bill and back-bill ones) that open a Bill Correction case: an analyst checks the read and rebills, or explains the bill. 0: disputes are only counted.
nodes.impact: Bill disputes become Bill Correction cases: wrong bills are rebilled on a check read (a credit on the next invoice), dunning pauses while they wait.

nodes.title: Dispute Hold Days
nodes.description: Collections pauses dunning on a disputed account until the dispute is decided, at most this long.
nodes.impact: How long a dispute can pause dunning: longer holds, fewer notices while the billing queue is behind.

nodes.title: Complaint Cases
nodes.description: A complaint the lines take opens a Customer Complaints case for the analysts to answer (one open complaint per account).
nodes.impact: Complaints become cases on the billing analysts' queue: less time for other billing work.

nodes.title: Frustration Threshold
nodes.description: Bad experiences (a hang-up after a long wait, an unresolved contact, a wait past long_wait_s, a complaint) before a customer pays later from then on. 0: never.
nodes.impact: Lower: more customers pay later after bad service (more overdue bills, notices and disconnections); 0 switches it off.

nodes.title: Long Wait S
nodes.description: A wait this long counts as a bad experience even when the call is answered.
nodes.impact: Shorter: more answered calls count as bad experiences, so more customers pay later.

nodes.title: Autopay Cancel Share
nodes.description: Share of frustrated customers on pre-authorized debit who cancel it and pay by hand from then on (later, and sometimes not at all).
nodes.impact: More frustrated customers leave pre-authorized debit and pay by hand: later payments, more reminders.

nodes.title: Enabled
nodes.description: Draw outages and leaks across the year.
nodes.impact: Draw the operations day's incidents for every day of the year: customers out lose their use and AMI meters go dark. Off: no outages, and outage and gas odour contacts are background only.

nodes.title: Storm Factor
nodes.description: Multiplies the chance that a day is a storm day.
nodes.impact: Multiplies the chance of a storm day: more overhead line faults, outages (use lost, a read missed when one falls inside) and outage reports, mostly May to September.

nodes.title: Incident Factor
nodes.description: Multiplies every incident rate (leaks, breaks, failures, faults).
nodes.impact: Multiplies every incident rate: more outages, main breaks and gas leaks, the use they cut and the contacts they bring.

nodes.title: Restore Factor
nodes.description: Multiplies the time to restore service.
nodes.impact: Multiplies the time to restore service: more use lost, more AMI reads falling inside an outage, and twice the outage reports past two hours.

nodes.title: Shift Start Hour
nodes.description: Crews start their day (local time, business days).
nodes.impact: When the business-day crews start. It moves when work is done in the day and which emergencies fall after hours (call-out and overtime).

nodes.title: Shift Hours
nodes.description: Hours in a crew's working day.
nodes.impact: Hours in a crew's day: every business-day crew's capacity. Shorter days build backlog, overdue work and overtime.

nodes.title: Routing
nodes.description: Crews drive the town's streets: from the depot in the morning, job to job by the fastest route (the operations driving speeds), and back at the end of the day. Of the jobs equally urgent and due, a crew takes the nearest next. On-call responders drive from the depot and back. Off, or in a town without streets: every visit adds travel_minutes.
nodes.impact: Crews drive the streets from the depot, job to job, nearest first: travel follows the town's size and layout. Off: a flat travel time per visit (usually more crew time, later work and slower emergency response).

nodes.title: Stop Minutes
nodes.description: With routing: parking, walking to the asset and setting up at each stop, added to the drive.
nodes.impact: Time at each stop on top of the drive (with routing): more fills the crews' day with fewer jobs.

nodes.title: Travel Minutes
nodes.description: Driving to the job and back, added to every visit without routing (and to the VEE field visits the run times).
nodes.impact: Without routing, driving to each job and back: more travel fills the crews' day with fewer jobs, and slows emergency response. VEE field visits use it always.

nodes.title: Callout Minutes
nodes.description: After hours, the time an on-call responder takes to get on the road.
nodes.impact: Time for an on-call responder to get on the road after hours: emergency response times at night and on weekends.

nodes.title: Overtime Max Hours
nodes.description: Most hours a crew works past its shift to finish same-day and overdue customer work (priority 1 and 2).
nodes.impact: Overtime per crew for customer work due today or overdue: more keeps disconnects, reconnects and move reads on time, at overtime cost.

nodes.title: Remote Switch Share
nodes.description: Share of AMI electric meters with a remote connect switch: their disconnects, reconnects and move reads need no truck.
nodes.impact: AMI electric meters with a remote switch: their disconnects and reconnects need no truck.

nodes.title: Seal Years Electric
nodes.description: Electric meter seal period: a lot whose seal expires this year is sampled.
nodes.impact: Electric seal period: picks which install year's lots are sampled this year (the meters' install cohorts set the volume).

nodes.title: Seal Years Gas
nodes.description: Gas meter seal period.
nodes.impact: Gas seal period: picks which install year's lots are sampled this year.

nodes.title: Seal Sample Size
nodes.description: Meters pulled and tested from each lot whose seal expires.
nodes.impact: Meters pulled from each expiring lot: more sample exchanges.

nodes.title: Seal Lot Pass Rate
nodes.description: Share of lots that pass compliance sampling and are resealed; a failed lot is exchanged meter by meter before its seal expires.
nodes.impact: Lots that pass sampling. A failed lot has every meter exchanged by 31 December: the biggest swing in meter work.

nodes.title: Battery Years
nodes.description: Radio module battery life on gas and water meters, AMI and AMR (they have no mains power).
nodes.impact: Module battery life: picks which install year's gas and water modules get new batteries this year.

nodes.title: Water Meter Life Years
nodes.description: Water meters this old or older are due for replacement.
nodes.impact: Water meters this old or older are due for replacement: a shorter life puts more cohorts in the backlog.

nodes.title: Dead Battery Miss
nodes.description: Share of reads a radio module misses once its battery has died (past its life and not replaced): estimates follow.
nodes.impact: Reads a module misses once its battery died (not replaced by its anniversary): estimates, estimation cases and contacts follow.

nodes.title: Failed Lot Drift
nodes.description: Under-registration of a failed seal lot's meters, from the failed test until each is exchanged.
nodes.impact: How much a failed seal lot's meters under-register until exchanged: less billed against the truth while the exchanges wait.

nodes.title: Old Water Meter Drift
nodes.description: Under-registration of water meters at or past their service life, until replaced (read at the start of the year).
nodes.impact: How much water meters past their life under-register until replaced: the revenue a replacement programme recovers.

nodes.title: Deferred Pole Failures
nodes.description: Chance a year that a pole found needing replacement fails once its replacement is overdue (ten times as likely on a storm day): an outage.
nodes.impact: How likely an overdue pole replacement fails: an outage (use lost, AMI meters dark), outage reports and repairs on the line crews.

nodes.title: Deferred Tree Faults
nodes.description: Chance on a storm day that an overhead span overdue for trimming faults: an outage.
nodes.impact: How likely a span overdue for trimming faults on a storm day: an outage (use lost, AMI meters dark) and outage reports.

nodes.title: Deferred Leak Escalation
nodes.description: Chance a year that a leak found by survey becomes a public gas leak (odour calls, an emergency) once its repair is overdue.
nodes.impact: How likely a surveyed leak overdue for repair becomes a public gas leak: odour calls and emergency response.

nodes.title: Renewed Main Break Factor
nodes.description: A renewed main's breaks and leaks, as a share of the cast-iron main's it replaced: from the day the construction crew finishes a segment.
nodes.impact: How much less a renewed main breaks and leaks than the cast iron it replaced: fewer main breaks and gas leaks (outages, contacts, repairs) after the construction crews renew it.

nodes.title: Construction Start Month
nodes.description: First month of the construction season (digging is frost-free).
nodes.impact: First month of the construction season: new services, upgrades, AMI conversion and main renewal wait for it.

nodes.title: Construction End Month
nodes.description: Last month of the construction season.
nodes.impact: Last month of the construction season: work not built by then waits for next year.

nodes.title: On-call responders
nodes.description: Gas odour and no-supply calls, any hour of any day.
nodes.impact: On-call responders: fewer stretch emergency response when emergencies overlap; the cost prices their time.
