nodes.title: Missed reads
nodes.description: Share of scheduled billing reads with no read taken: AMI dropouts, drive-by misses, no access.
nodes.formula: missed reads ÷ scheduled reads, year to date

nodes.title: Estimated reads
nodes.description: Share of scheduled billing reads released to billing as an estimate rather than an actual read.
nodes.formula: estimated releases ÷ scheduled reads, year to date

nodes.title: Reads released promptly
nodes.description: Share of held reads (a case raised on them) that were released to billing within the window, counted from the scheduled read day.
nodes.formula: held reads released within kpi.read_release_days ÷ held reads released

nodes.title: Auto-accepted reads
nodes.description: Share of actual reads VEE accepted without a person looking.
nodes.formula: auto-accepted ÷ actual reads

nodes.title: VEE exceptions
nodes.description: Cases VEE's own tests raised (high, low, zero and erratic use, register regression, odd periods, persistent low use, vacant but consuming), per 1,000 accounts a year.
nodes.formula: VEE cases ÷ accounts × 1,000, annualised

nodes.title: VEE precision
nodes.description: Of the reads VEE flagged, the share that were real anomalies in the simulation's truth.
nodes.formula: flagged and anomalous ÷ flagged

nodes.title: VEE recall
nodes.description: Of the real anomalies among actual reads, the share VEE flagged.
nodes.formula: flagged and anomalous ÷ anomalous

nodes.title: Exceptions, every case
nodes.description: Every clarification case opened, per 1,000 accounts a year: missed reads, VEE exceptions, billing blocks, disputes and complaints, whoever resolved them.
nodes.formula: cases opened ÷ accounts × 1,000, annualised

nodes.title: Exceptions a person worked
nodes.description: Cases an analyst, a supervisor or you touched, per 1,000 accounts a year: what a billing team counts as its exceptions, automation's own resolutions left out.
nodes.formula: cases a person touched ÷ accounts × 1,000, annualised

nodes.title: Open cases
nodes.description: Cases open at the view date, per 1,000 accounts.
nodes.formula: open cases ÷ accounts × 1,000

nodes.title: Days to release a held read
nodes.description: Average calendar days from the scheduled read to the day its case released it to billing, for cases resolved year to date.
nodes.formula: mean(release day − scheduled read day)

nodes.title: Cases resolved in time
nodes.description: Share of cases raised year to date that closed within the window, in business days from being raised; a case still open counts as not in time.
nodes.formula: cases closed within kpi.case_resolution_days ÷ cases raised

nodes.title: Truck rolls
nodes.description: Field visits made for cases (check reads, no-access visits, meter faults), per 1,000 accounts a year.
nodes.formula: truck rolls ÷ accounts × 1,000, annualised

nodes.title: Invoices on time
nodes.description: Scheduled account-month cycles with every due service issued within the operational invoice window. Includes print lag; pending cycles are not on time. Each service uses its own scheduled read day.
nodes.formula: account-cycles fully issued within kpi.on_time_bill_days ÷ scheduled account-cycles

nodes.title: Invoice timeliness
nodes.description: Scheduled account-month cycles with every due service issued within the invoice timeliness target. Includes cycles held before an invoice exists and print lag. Pending cycles are not yet timely; Delayed invoices counts them late only after the deadline expires.
nodes.formula: account-cycles fully issued within kpi.timely_invoice_days ÷ scheduled account-cycles

nodes.title: Invoice cycles affected by billing checks
nodes.description: Scheduled account-month cycles with at least one billing-document check raised, even if later released. Multiple service documents count once; this tracks upstream causes of invoice holds.
nodes.formula: account-cycles with a billing check ÷ scheduled account-cycles

nodes.title: Invoice amount error
nodes.description: Absolute net invoice error against simulated truth for invoices issued in the reporting window. Corrective invoice truth includes the credit for the previously invoiced version.
nodes.formula: Σ|net invoice total − net truth total| ÷ Σ|net invoice total|

nodes.title: Days to invoice issue
nodes.description: Average elapsed calendar days from the last scheduled read an invoice covers to its issue, including print lag. Only invoices issued by the view date count; issue cannot precede creation.
nodes.formula: mean(max(created, planned issue) − last scheduled read day)

nodes.title: Days to pay
nodes.description: Average days from an invoice's issue to its payment in full, for invoices paid year to date. Payer behaviour is a town setting (on-time and late payer shares), not a run lever.
nodes.formula: mean(paid − issued)

nodes.title: Invoices paid on time
nodes.description: Share of invoices whose due date (plus the grace window) has passed that were settled in full by then.
nodes.formula: invoices paid by due + kpi.payment_grace_days ÷ invoices past that date

nodes.title: Cash collected
nodes.description: Payments received year to date as a share of the amount invoiced.
nodes.formula: collected ÷ invoiced

nodes.title: Overdue receivable
nodes.description: Of the money owed at the view date, the share past its due date.
nodes.formula: overdue ÷ receivable

nodes.title: Disconnections
nodes.description: Services disconnected for non-payment, per 1,000 accounts a year.
nodes.formula: disconnected ÷ accounts × 1,000, annualised

nodes.title: Calls answered in target
nodes.description: Share of answered contacts whose wait was within the day's service target.
nodes.formula: answered within contact.service_target_s ÷ answered

nodes.title: Calls hung up
nodes.description: Share of contacts that reached the queue and hung up before an agent answered.
nodes.formula: abandoned ÷ (abandoned + answered)

nodes.title: Contacts
nodes.description: Contacts of every kind (self-served, answered, callbacks, abandoned), per 1,000 accounts a year.
nodes.formula: contacts ÷ accounts × 1,000, annualised

nodes.title: Resolved first time
nodes.description: Share of contacts resolved on the first attempt, self-served or answered, not a repeat.
nodes.formula: resolved first ÷ contacts

nodes.title: Field work on time
nodes.description: Share of completed field orders that met their target: arrival for emergencies, completion for the rest.
nodes.formula: orders that met their due time ÷ orders completed

nodes.title: Field orders open
nodes.description: Released field orders not yet done at the view date, per 1,000 accounts.
nodes.formula: open orders ÷ accounts × 1,000

nodes.title: Emergency response
nodes.description: Average minutes from an emergency order (gas odour, no supply) to the crew's arrival.
nodes.formula: mean(arrive − created) for emergency orders

nodes.title: Customer minutes without service
nodes.description: Minutes of interrupted service per customer over the year's outages and leaks, all utilities together.
nodes.formula: Σ customer-minutes interrupted ÷ customers

nodes.title: Process cost per account
nodes.description: The year's meter-to-cash process cost (people, systems, customer effects, reads) per account.
nodes.formula: cost total ÷ accounts

nodes.title: Carrying cost per account
nodes.description: Money held up in unreleased reads, unbilled periods and unpaid invoices, priced at the carry rate, per account.
nodes.formula: (case carry + billing carry + receivable carry) ÷ accounts

nodes.title: Active services
nodes.description: Supply contracts active on the view date. A multi-service account contributes one contract per service.
nodes.formula: count(active supply contracts)

nodes.title: Active service setup defects
nodes.description: Active contracts with a missing account or installation, a premise mismatch, or overlapping active contracts for one installation.
nodes.formula: count(active contracts failing reference or uniqueness checks)

nodes.title: Move-ins
nodes.description: Premises with a recorded move-in date this year through the view date.
nodes.formula: count(0 ≤ move-in day ≤ view day)

nodes.title: Move-outs
nodes.description: Premises with a recorded move-out date this year through the view date.
nodes.formula: count(0 ≤ move-out day ≤ view day)

nodes.title: Invoice net-term mismatches
nodes.description: Created invoices whose original due date minus issue date differs from the configured payment term. Later payment arrangements do not count as defects.
nodes.formula: invoices with original due − issued ≠ configured due days ÷ created invoices

nodes.title: Delayed invoices
nodes.description: Scheduled account-month cycles with any service invoiced after its deadline, or still awaiting issue after that deadline. Includes reads and billing documents held upstream, and invoice print lag. Each service uses its own scheduled read day; an account-cycle is counted once.
nodes.formula: late or overdue unissued account-cycles ÷ scheduled account-cycles

nodes.title: Estimated invoices
nodes.description: Issued invoices containing at least one estimated service charge. A multi-service invoice counts once. Subsequent reversals do not rewrite what was originally issued.
nodes.formula: issued invoices containing an estimated charge ÷ issued invoices

nodes.title: Move-boundary invoices estimated
nodes.description: Issued invoices containing an estimated service period spanning a recorded move-in or move-out, among invoices with such a boundary. This is not a separate first/final settlement workflow.
nodes.formula: issued invoices with an estimated move-boundary charge ÷ issued move-boundary invoices

nodes.title: Consecutive estimated invoices
nodes.description: Issued invoices containing an estimated charge for a month whose immediately preceding account-month was also estimated on a previously issued invoice. Missing months break the sequence; multiple services, corrective versions and two months on one invoice do not add consecutive cycles. Previously issued corrections update the preceding cycle for later invoices.
nodes.formula: issued invoices continuing a 2+ month estimate sequence ÷ issued invoices

nodes.title: Consecutive zero-use invoices
nodes.description: Issued invoices with all-zero import and export charges whose preceding account-month on a previously issued invoice was also all zero. Missing months break the sequence. Fixed charges may still apply.
nodes.formula: issued invoices continuing a 2+ month zero-use sequence ÷ issued invoices

nodes.title: Invoice period defects
nodes.description: Issued invoices containing a non-finite, non-positive or overlapping service period for the same installation and account. Corrective versions of the same period and different services are not overlaps.
nodes.formula: issued invoices with a defective service period ÷ issued invoices

nodes.title: Invoice due-date defects
nodes.description: Created invoices with missing/non-finite issue or due dates, or an original due date before issue.
nodes.formula: invoices with invalid original due or issue dates ÷ created invoices

nodes.title: Corrective invoices
nodes.description: Issued invoices correcting a charge on a previously issued invoice. Document corrections made before first issue are excluded; their reversals remain visible in billing documents.
nodes.formula: issued invoices replacing a previously invoiced charge ÷ issued invoices

nodes.title: Cycles with multiple invoices
nodes.description: Account/cycle-month combinations represented on more than one issued invoice. Staggered services and corrective invoices can legitimately produce this; it is an audit indicator.
nodes.formula: account/cycle combinations with 2+ invoices ÷ invoiced account/cycle combinations

nodes.title: Invoices without a customer charge
nodes.description: Issued invoices with no non-zero fixed charge across their service lines, reconstructed from the tariff calculation. Zero-fixed-charge tariffs are included; this does not detect an external print omission.
nodes.formula: issued invoices with no non-zero computed fixed charge ÷ issued invoices

nodes.title: Invoices with move-boundary prorated charges
nodes.description: Issued invoices with at least one move-boundary charge prorated by read-period duration. Each invoice counts once. Proration uses read days, not a separate move settlement period.
nodes.formula: count(issued invoices with a non-zero move-boundary fixed charge)

nodes.title: Invoices awaiting issue
nodes.description: Invoices already created whose planned issue day is after the view date. This is print-lag workload; the engine does not record actual print completion.
nodes.formula: count(created invoices with planned issue after view time)

nodes.title: Billing exceptions raised
nodes.description: Billing-check and billing-dispute cases raised this year through the view date, including subsequently resolved cases. This is the model equivalent of a billing exception workload, not SAP BPEM telemetry.
nodes.formula: count(year-to-date billing check and dispute cases)

nodes.title: Active billing-document blocks
nodes.description: Current documents with a billing case that remain unreleased at the view date. Account-level invoice holds are counted separately.
nodes.formula: count(current case-blocked documents not released by view time)

nodes.title: Active invoice holds
nodes.description: Account-level invoice holds in force at the view date.
nodes.formula: count(hold start ≤ view time < hold end)

nodes.title: Invoiced accounts without a linked meter
nodes.description: Active accounts with invoices issued this year that have no meter linked through an active supply contract on the view date. This is a reference-integrity check, not a zero-consumption check.
nodes.formula: count(active invoiced accounts without a current linked meter)

nodes.title: Active read-release blocks
nodes.description: Scheduled active register periods whose read was attempted, has a case, and remains unreleased. These are VEE/review holds; administrative meter-reading blocks are not separately modelled.
nodes.formula: count(attempted register periods with a case and release after view time)

nodes.title: Open scheduled reads
nodes.description: Scheduled active register periods due by the view date without a released value, including missing and held reads. Future and service-off periods are excluded.
nodes.formula: count(due active register periods with release after view time)

nodes.title: Reads taken early
nodes.description: Actual observations taken on a calendar day before the scheduled read day. Estimates and missing observations are excluded.
nodes.formula: early actual observations ÷ actual observations taken by view time

nodes.title: Reads taken late
nodes.description: Actual observations taken on a calendar day after the scheduled read day. Same-day time-of-day differences do not count as late.
nodes.formula: late actual observations ÷ actual observations taken by view time

nodes.title: Open implausible-read cases
nodes.description: Unresolved VEE anomaly cases at the view date. Missing-read, billing, field-order and invoice-hold cases are excluded.
nodes.formula: count(open VEE anomaly cases)

nodes.title: Active accounts without a linked meter
nodes.description: Active accounts without a meter linked through an active contract, installation and service point. An unmetered tariff may be intentional; review the account.
nodes.formula: count(active accounts with no current meter association)

nodes.title: Meters without an active account
nodes.description: Installed active meter records with no active supply contract linked to a known active account. Vacancies can be legitimate; retired meters are excluded.
nodes.formula: count(active installed meters with no active account association)

edges.note: Regenerating the town redraws households; geometry is not a calibrated usage lever.

explanation.summary: The generated lots and buildings become the premises on which household attributes are drawn.
steps: Building type and construction era constrain the household and building attributes.
Regenerating the town redraws these records; changing geometry is not a calibrated consumption adjustment.

explanation.summary: Premises supply the service locations for customers, accounts and utility contracts.
steps: Customer generation attaches the applicable services and contracts to those premises.
An account can cover more than one service; homes and accounts are not interchangeable counts.

explanation.summary: Occupants, floor area, heating type, appliances and occupancy determine the baseline demand profile.
explanation.formula: base electricity (kWh/day) = (4 + 0.03 × floor area + 1.5 × occupants) × occupancy factor
steps: The occupancy factor is 1 when occupied and 0.12 otherwise for this electric base load.
Heating, cooling, EVs, pools and solar add their own terms. Water and gas have separate equations.

explanation.summary: The connected premises and their estimated loads feed the network flow model.
steps: Loads are aggregated onto connected electrical, gas and water equipment.
The model uses these demands to calculate loading, service voltage and pressure on the operations map.

explanation.summary: Temperature drives heating and cooling demand before the meter observes consumption.
explanation.formula: daily heating demand = building heat-loss coefficient × monthly mean heating degrees per day
steps: Building heat loss uses floor area and construction era.
Heating technology converts heat demand to electricity or gas; cooling demand uses the monthly mean cooling degrees per day.

explanation.summary: Cold weather increases the probability that a scheduled read is missed.
explanation.formula:
cold = clamp((−10 − temperature °C) / 10, 0, 1.5)
miss probability = min(1, base miss probability × (1 + cold))
steps: The base probability depends on AMI, AMR or manual reading and repeat no-access history.
A deterministic draw is compared with this probability; outages, dead batteries and episodes can also force a miss.

explanation.summary: Storm-day assumptions change the annual incident draws and the interruptions they produce.
steps: Storms create opportunities for overhead line faults.
The annual outage model applies its storm and incident factors to the background hazard model.
conditions: Annual outages must be enabled.

explanation.summary: Service contracts link customer accounts to the installations and registers they are billed for.
steps: The run builds account/contract/installation mappings from the town snapshot.
Service and contract dates determine the applicable account for a billing period.

explanation.summary: A premise’s billing-cycle portion supplies its scheduled business day in each month.
explanation.formula: scheduled date = business_days_in_month[min(max(portion, 1), number_of_business_days) − 1]
steps: The run carries the premise billing cycle onto its meter registers.
The business-day calendar excludes weekends and Ontario holidays; an oversized portion uses the last business day.

explanation.summary: The account’s payer profile and payment method determine how its invoices enter payment and collection processing.
steps: On-time, late and non-paying behaviour is assigned to customers when the town is built.
Due dates and the collections rules then determine receipts, reminders, arrangements and possible disconnection.

explanation.summary: Each register inherits its premise’s read date; its technology determines the time of the read attempt.
explanation.formula: read timestamp = scheduled read day + technology-specific read hour / 24
steps: The technology’s base hour is spread using a deterministic household hash.

explanation.summary: Technology and register characteristics control how consumption becomes an observed reading.
steps: AMI, drive-by AMR and manual meters use different miss probabilities and attempt times.
Register modulus controls rollover; device faults, batteries and communications can alter or suppress the observation.

explanation.summary: The installed device population supplies the meters eligible for checks, exchanges and technology conversion.
steps: Field-work types select eligible devices and create dated work orders.
A completed device change affects later readings through the device-work feedback link.

explanation.summary: Equipment, connectivity and loading determine where failures can occur and which premises are affected.
steps: Hazards use asset counts or lengths, with equipment-specific adjustments.
Dispatch and restoration use network connectivity; back-feed checks use loading and voltage limits.

explanation.summary: Fault, isolation and restoration events create service-loss intervals for the affected premises.
steps: Dispatch, travel, repair and switching determine the interval boundaries.
A tie restoration can end some customers’ interruptions before the original repair finishes.

explanation.summary: The operations-day summaries total the duration and customer impact of the day’s service interruptions.
explanation.formula: customer-minutes = Σ(affected customers × interruption minutes)
conditions: These are operations-day results. They are not automatically annual-run results.

explanation.summary: Dispatch and incident timestamps supply response and restoration measures for the operations day.
steps: Gas incidents compare crew response time with the configured response target.
Incident summaries also record detection, isolation, repair and restoration events.

edges.note: Only interruptions carried from the operations day into the run.

explanation.summary: An explicitly carried operations day contributes its service-loss intervals to the annual run.
steps: The annual run consumes the carried intervals for the affected premises.
Carried days replace the corresponding background outage day, avoiding duplicate incident generation.
conditions: Requires carrying the operations day into the run; merely viewing or editing the map does not do this.

explanation.summary: The annual hazard model converts daily incidents into dated service-loss intervals.
steps: Asset type and location determine the affected premises; restoration assumptions determine duration.
Annual incident consequences use their own travel/restoration model, not the map’s live crew queue.
conditions: Annual outages must be enabled. Carried operations days replace background days.

explanation.summary: Service interruptions reduce delivered consumption; electricity or collector outages can also prevent an AMI read.
steps: Lost service subtracts the corresponding consumption from the register advance.
A dark electric AMI meter or muted collector can force a missing observation at the scheduled attempt.

explanation.summary: An incident can generate contacts from affected customers using its contact-reason probability.
explanation.formula: contact probability = min(1, reason.per_event × context multiplier × contact.volume_factor)
steps: The reason and incident context determine the multiplier; the contact model then selects channel and handles the queue.

explanation.summary: Incident consequences can request emergency field response for affected premises.
steps: The field model creates work with an emergency type, location and due time.
Available crews and travel determine arrival; arrival is the emergency service-target milestone.

explanation.summary: The read schedule decides when the engine attempts each register’s monthly reading.
explanation.formula: read timestamp = scheduled read day + read hour / 24
steps: The premise billing cycle selects a business day in the month.
Consumption is accumulated to that timestamp, then technology, weather, access and device conditions decide the observation.
conditions: A scheduled attempt does not guarantee a successful or released read.

explanation.summary: Underlying consumption supplies the true cumulative register before observation errors and misses.
explanation.formula: true register = initial register + normal consumption advance + consumption adjustments
steps: Adjustments include consumption lost during interruptions and extra consumption such as leaks.
The observation then applies meter behaviour, rollover and reading errors; a miss is stored as a missing value.

explanation.summary: The consumption baseline is the quantity on which injected leaks and meter faults act.
steps: Physical extra usage changes truth; observation faults can change what the meter reports without making the same change to truth.
The engine retains that distinction to assess VEE detection and billing error.

explanation.summary: Each attempted read writes the observed value and the attempt’s status into the period’s register records.
steps: Successful attempts store a numeric observation; missed attempts store a missing observation.
Scheduled time and true consumption remain available for validation and measurement.

explanation.summary: Injected anomalies modify the physical advance, the meter observation, or its availability.
steps: Leaks affect actual usage; meter and manual-reading errors affect the observation according to their fault type.
Truth labels are retained for precision/recall evaluation instead of treating every validation flag as a genuine error.

explanation.summary: Validation compares observed consumption with expected consumption and checks plausibility and reading history.
explanation.formula:
observed consumption = current observation − previous register
if rollover is recognised: consumption += register modulus
steps: The batch supplies days, expected usage, units, occupancy, moves, prior exceptions and manual-reading status.
VEE rules produce reason codes, confidence and a disposition; a missing observation follows the missing-read/estimate path.

explanation.summary: Validation records its reason codes, confidence and disposition for each evaluated read.
explanation.formula: confidence = clamp(1 − 2 × sum(test risks), 0, 1)
steps: Register regression is rejected. Otherwise confidence at/above accept_confidence is accepted; below reject_confidence is rejected.
Remaining reads escalate when impact reaches escalate_impact, or go to review otherwise.
Evaluation against injected truth identifies true positives, false positives and false negatives.

explanation.summary: A read that cannot pass directly opens a clarification case or joins existing held work.
steps: The case stores the read period, reason, confidence and required disposition.
Existing open work can keep later reads held on the same register.

explanation.summary: A clean accepted observation is made available to billing without analyst work.
explanation.formula: direct release: observation present AND disposition = accept AND no open case
steps: This clean-read path records release at day + 18.5/24.
Held reads require resolution through automation, casework or a field outcome before billing can use them.

explanation.summary: Open, eligible cases enter the analyst, supervisor or automation workflow.
explanation.formula: analyst capacity (minutes/business day) = analysts × analyst_hours_per_day × 60
steps: Assignment consumes case review time from daily capacity.
Ownership, automation status, billing-queue rules and escalation determine which cases each workflow can take.

explanation.summary: Resolving held read work writes the accepted or estimated value and its release timestamp.
steps: The resolution method determines the value: accept, correct, estimate or a field-confirmed reading.
Billing can proceed once all required registers for an installation’s period are released.

edges.note: Cases sent for field investigation.

explanation.summary: An escalated clarification case can request a field investigation instead of being resolved at the desk.
steps: Disposition and financial impact help determine escalation.
The request waits for field capacity; related read cases at one premise can share a visit.
conditions: Only cases actually referred to field investigation take this path.

explanation.summary: Released register values supply billable consumption for the installation and period.
steps: Billing waits until every required register for the period is ready.
Register differences and device adjustments produce import/export quantities; the applicable tariff prices them.

explanation.summary: Tariff calculation creates a billing document, then billing checks decide whether to release or hold it.
explanation.formula: high-bill check: total > max(high_bill_ratio × expected total, expected total + high_bill_min)
steps: Other checks include true-up, rate class, first-bill limits and large credits.
The document records billed, expected and true totals, its creation time, and any case/release time.

explanation.summary: Released, uninvoiced billing documents are grouped by account into an invoice.
explanation.formula: invoice total = Σ included document totals − applicable reversal credits
steps: Invoice processing runs at 20:00 on the queued business day and respects account invoice holds.
The invoice creation timestamp differs from its issue date: print lag delays issue; due days are added to issue.

edges.note: A billing check or outsort raises a clarification case.

explanation.summary: A failed billing check creates a billing clarification case and holds the document.
steps: True-up, rate-class, high-bill and credit checks can trigger this path.
A later release can unblock invoicing, but the document still counts as having raised a billing case.
conditions: Only documents that fail a billing check take this path.

explanation.summary: Invoice amount, issue date, due date and account identity start the payment and collection lifecycle.
explanation.formula: due date = issue date + customers_billing.due_days
steps: Payer behaviour schedules payment; outstanding balances progress through configured reminders and collection stages.

explanation.summary: Payment and collection events update receipts, outstanding balances and service status.
steps: Records distinguish payment in full, notices, arrangements and disconnection activity.
Their timestamps allow cash measures to be evaluated at the selected view date.

explanation.summary: Invoice events can generate billing-related customer contacts.
explanation.formula: contact probability = min(1, reason.per_event × context multiplier × contact.volume_factor)
steps: Invoice amount and billing context select reasons such as a high bill or a billing question.
The contact model samples whether the customer contacts the utility, then applies channel and queue rules.

explanation.summary: Contact demand is turned into dated self-service, answered, abandoned and repeat-contact records.
steps: Self-service attempts can resolve a contact before it reaches an agent.
Staffing, opening hours, handling time and customer patience determine queue wait and abandonment; outcomes can schedule callbacks or repeats.

edges.note: Dispute or complaint referrals are enabled and triggered.

explanation.summary: Eligible dispute and complaint outcomes create follow-up clarification cases.
steps: Dispute referral uses its configured probability; repeated unresolved interactions can produce a complaint.
conditions: The corresponding dispute/complaint referrals must be enabled and their trigger must occur.

edges.note: Contact outcomes trigger payment delay, arrangements or autopay cancellation.

explanation.summary: Contact outcomes can change collection handling and future payment behaviour.
steps: A dispute can hold collections; a resolved interaction may establish a payment arrangement.
Bad experiences can trigger the configured payment-delay or autopay-cancellation feedback.
conditions: Only outcomes that trigger the enabled feedback rules change the collection path.

explanation.summary: The field engine schedules work against crew availability and records dispatch, arrival and completion.
steps: Work type supplies service duration and target; travel and available crew time determine timing.
Order records retain release, creation, due, arrival and completion timestamps for service and backlog measures.

edges.note: A completed check read or meter investigation releases held work.

explanation.summary: A completed check read or investigation can resolve the read work that caused the visit.
steps: The field-confirmed result supplies the correction or release for held work.
Other order types do not automatically release reads.
conditions: Requires a completed visit connected to held read work.

edges.note: Device work changes later reads; for example, a meter exchange or AMI conversion.

explanation.summary: Completed device work changes the device state used by later readings.
steps: An exchange repairs/replaces the device; an AMI conversion changes the reading technology.
The change takes effect from the work outcome, not retrospectively across the whole year.
conditions: Only work types with a device effect update the meter.

explanation.summary: Recorded reads are priced with the cost for their reading technology.
explanation.formula: read cost = Σ(read count by technology × configured cost per read)

explanation.summary: Case activity events accumulate the engine’s people, system and customer-effect costs.
explanation.formula: case process cost = Σ(cost of recorded case events)
steps: Cost follows recorded work; analyst headcount is not simply multiplied by an annual salary in this measure.

explanation.summary: Billing, invoice and payment activities contribute their recorded event costs to the meter-to-cash total.
explanation.formula: process cost = case activity cost + billing/payment activity cost + read cost
conditions: Contact-centre and field labour/materials are reported separately from this total.

explanation.summary: Contact statistics price staff time, self-service and abandoned contacts separately.
explanation.formula: contact cost = staff hours × hourly cost + self-served count × self-serve cost + abandoned count × abandonment cost + dispatch handling cost
steps: Dispatch handling time is converted from seconds to hours before applying the hourly rate.

explanation.summary: Field statistics price recorded labour and materials by crew and work type.
explanation.formula: field cost = regular labour cost + overtime labour cost + materials
steps: Crew hourly rates and overtime factors price labour; the work type supplies materials per order.

explanation.summary: Unreleased read work accumulates delay cost from its scheduled day until resolution or the view date.
explanation.formula: case carry = Σ(max(0, end − max(scheduled day, 0)) × carry_rate_per_day)
steps: End is resolution by the view date, otherwise the view date.
This applies to read-holding cases, not every work-order case.

explanation.summary: The read periods covered by invoiced documents supply the start of the billing-delay cost.
explanation.formula: billing carry per invoice = max(0, invoice created − last scheduled read day) × carry_rate_per_day
steps: The last scheduled day is taken across that invoice’s billing documents.

explanation.summary: Invoice creation and issue dates mark billing delay and the start of receivable delay.
explanation.formula: receivable carry = Σ(max(0, end − max(issue date, 0)) × carry_rate_per_day × receivable_carry_ratio)
steps: End is payment by the view date, otherwise the view date.
This engine applies a daily cost per invoice; it does not multiply this term by the invoice balance.

explanation.summary: Payment in full stops the invoice’s receivable-delay clock.
explanation.formula: end of receivable delay = payment time if paid by view date; otherwise view date
steps: The resulting elapsed days are priced at carry_rate_per_day × receivable_carry_ratio.

reaches.year: Changes the meter-to-cash year directly, on the same town.
reaches.town: Changes the customers, usage, routes or prices the year replays. Builds a new town.
reaches.shape: Map shape. Rearranges the town; the year moves only because homes are drawn again (seed-sized noise).
reaches.operations: The operations day on the map. Reaches the year only through interruptions you carry into a run.
reaches.display: Display only: labels, units, clocks or default dates. No result changes.
